title: Writing and Evaluating Expressions; Expressions vs. Equations
seo_title: Grade 6 Expressions and Equations Worksheets: Write and Evaluate (TEKS 6.7B, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.7B distinguish between expressions and equations verbally, numerically, and algebraically
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.7B: write expressions from words, parts of an expression, expression or equation, evaluate expressions, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: An expression has no equal sign; an equation does.
key_sub: 3n + 5 is an expression. 3n + 5 = 20 is an equation.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An expression is a math phrase with numbers, variables and operations, but no equal sign: 3n + 5.
  • An equation says two expressions are equal: 3n + 5 = 20.
  • Terms are separated by + or −. A coefficient multiplies a variable; a constant stands alone.
  • To evaluate, substitute the value and follow the order of operations.

Examples

Example

Write: 4 less than twice a number n

twice n = 2n

4 less than: subtract 4

Answer: 2n − 4

Example

Evaluate 3n + 5 when n = 6

3 × 6 = 18

18 + 5

Answer: 23

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 3 less than n as 3 − nLess than reverses the order: n − 3.
Calling 3n + 5 an equationNo equal sign means it is an expression.
Evaluating 3n as 36 when n = 63n means 3 × n = 18.

faq.a: Distinguish between expressions and equations verbally, numerically and algebraically.

faq.q: Can an equation have no variable?
faq.a: Yes. 4 × 5 = 20 is an equation because it has an equal sign.
The number multiplied by a variable, like 7 in 7y.

faq.q: Do I use the order of operations when evaluating?
faq.a: Yes. Substitute first, then follow the order of operations.

items.q: What does 3n mean?
items.e: A number written right next to a letter means multiply: 3n = 3 × n. So when n = 5, 3n = 3 × 5 = 15, not 35.

items.q: Which expression means 6 more than m?
items.e: “More than” means add: start with m and add 6, so m + 6. 6m would mean 6 × m.

items.q: Which expression means the product of 3 and t?
items.e: “Product” means multiply: 3 × t. A number next to a letter means multiply, so write 3t.

items.q: Which expression means 3 less than q?
items.e: “3 less than q” starts with q and takes 3 away: q − 3. 3 − q has the order backward.

items.q: Which expression means the sum of k and 9?
items.e: “Sum” means add: k + 9. 9k is a product, not a sum.

items.q: Which expression means c divided by 3?
items.e: The number being divided comes first: c ÷ 3. 3 ÷ c divides 3 by c, which is different.

items.q: Which expression means twice h?
items.e: “Twice” means 2 times: 2 × h = 2h. h2 means h × h, not 2 × h.

items.q: Which expression means p decreased by 8?
items.e: “Decreased by 8” means take 8 away from p: p − 8. 8 − p has the order backward.

items.q: Which expression means d squared?
items.e: “Squared” means multiply the number by itself: d × d = d2. 2d means 2 × d, which is a different value.

items.q: Which expression means subtract b from 23?
items.e: “Subtract b from 23” means start with 23 and take b away: 23 − b, not b − 23.

items.q: Which expression means z increased by 5?
items.e: “Increased by” means add: z + 5. 5z would mean 5 × z.

items.q: Which expression means half of r?
items.e: Half of a number means divide it by 2: r ÷ 2. 2r would be twice the number.

items.q: Which expression means the quotient of 7 and x?
items.e: “Quotient” means divide, and the first number named is divided: 7 ÷ x. x ÷ 7 has the order backward.

items.q: Which expression means y cubed?
items.e: “Cubed” means use the number as a factor 3 times: y × y × y = y3. 3y means 3 × y.

items.q: Which expression means 5 times the sum of g and 10?
items.e: The sum g + 10 must be found first, so it goes in parentheses: 5(g + 10). 5g + 10 multiplies only g by 5.

items.q: Which expression means 4 more than 8 times w?
items.e: 8 times w is 8w. 4 more than that means add 4: 8w + 4. No parentheses are needed, because you multiply first anyway.

items.q: Which expression means 7 fewer than the product of 8 and n?
items.e: The product of 8 and n is 8n. “7 fewer than” it means take 7 away: 8n − 7, not 7 − 8n.

items.q: Which expression means triple m, then subtract 12?
items.e: Triple means 3 times: 3m. Then subtract 12: 3m − 12. m3 − 12 would cube m, not triple it.

items.q: Which expression means the quotient of t and 3, plus 2?
items.e: The quotient of t and 3 is t ÷ 3. Then add 2: t ÷ 3 + 2. t ÷ (3 + 2) would add 3 + 2 first.

items.q: Which expression means the sum of q and d, divided by 3?
items.e: The whole sum is divided, so it goes in parentheses: (q + d) ÷ 3. q + d ÷ 3 would divide only d by 3.

items.q: How many terms are in 4x + 7y + 2?
items.e: Terms are the parts joined by + or −: 4x, 7y and 2. That is 3 terms.

items.q: What is the coefficient of m in 7m + 15?
items.e: The coefficient is the number multiplied by the variable: 7m means 7 × m, so it is 7. 15 is the constant.

items.q: What is the constant in 9k + 10?
items.e: The constant is the term with no variable. It always stays 10. 9 is the coefficient of k.

items.q: What is the coefficient of p in p + 5?
items.e: p means 1 × p, so its coefficient is 1, even though the 1 is not written.

items.q: What are the terms of 11 + 3t?
items.e: Terms are separated by + or −. 3t is one term (3 × t), so the terms are 11 and 3t.

items.q: Which description fits 2(8 + 7)?
items.e: The last step is to multiply 2 by (8 + 7), so 2(8 + 7) is a product. Its two factors are 2 and (8 + 7).

items.q: In 2(8 + 7), how can you describe the factor (8 + 7)?
items.e: (8 + 7) is one factor of the product, and it is also a sum of the two terms 8 and 7. It equals 15.

items.q: Look at the last step. What kind of expression is (x + 7) ÷ 4?
items.e: The last step is to divide the sum by 4, so the whole expression is a quotient.

items.q: Look at the last step. What kind of expression is 4y − 7?
items.e: 4y is a product, but the last step is to subtract, so the whole expression is a difference.

items.q: Look at the last step. What kind of expression is 3(w − 4)?
items.e: The parentheses are worked first, and the last step is to multiply, so the whole expression is a product.

items.q: Look at the last step. What kind of expression is 14 + 2n?
items.e: 2n is a product, but the last step is to add, so the whole expression is a sum.

items.q: In 8x + 3y + 11, what is the coefficient of y?
items.e: The coefficient of y is the number multiplied by y: 3y. 8 goes with x, and 11 is the constant.

items.q: Which expression has a coefficient of 4 and a constant of 9?
items.e: In 4x + 9, 4 is multiplied by x (the coefficient) and 9 stands alone (the constant). In 9x + 4, 9 is the coefficient.

items.q: Which expression has 3 terms?
items.e: x + 2y + 7 has the terms x, 2y and 7. 2(x + 7) is one product (2 terms inside the parentheses), 8xy is 1 term, and 5x + 1 has 2 terms.

items.q: Which words match 6n + 10?
items.e: 6n is 6 times n. Adding 10 makes it 10 more. “6 times the sum” would need parentheses: 6(n + 10).

items.q: Which words match y − 9?
items.e: y − 9 starts with y and takes 9 away, so it is 9 less than y. “y less than 9” would be 9 − y.

items.q: Which words match 6(x − 3)?
items.e: The parentheses hold the difference x − 3, and it is multiplied by 6. “3 less than 6 times x” would be 6x − 3, with no parentheses.

items.q: Which words match k ÷ 6?
items.e: k ÷ 6 divides k by 6, so it is the quotient of k and 6. The order matters: 6 ÷ k is different.

items.q: What is the coefficient in 7x2 + 10?
items.e: 7x2 means 7 × x × x. The coefficient is 7. The small 2 is the exponent, and 10 is the constant.

items.q: Camila says the constant in 14 + 8n is 8. Is she right?
items.e: The constant is the term with no variable, which is 14. 8 is the coefficient of n. The order of the terms does not matter.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: x − 1 = 18.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: a ÷ 7 = 8.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: n = 39.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: y − 14.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: 22 + 10 × 11.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: n − 25.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: y − 17 = 23.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: k = 22.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: 2 + 5 × 6.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: x = 81.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: n − 4 = 36.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: n − 29.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: 7 + 5 × 6.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: 5k + 2 = 13.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: k − 14 = 90.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: n ÷ 4.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: x ÷ 5 = 27.

items.q: Which of these is an expression, not an equation?
items.e: An expression has no equal sign: k ÷ 4.

items.q: Which of these is an equation?
items.e: An equation has an equal sign that shows two amounts are equal: t − 3 = 18.

items.q: What is the value of 7n when n = 8?
items.e: Replace n with 8: 7 × 8 = 56. Not 78: that reads 7n as the number 78.

items.q: Evaluate 8n + 2 when n = 7.
items.e: Replace n with 7: 8 × 7 + 2 = 56 + 2 = 58. Not 89: that reads 8n as the number 87.

items.q: Find the value of 4n − 6 when n = 7.
items.e: Replace n with 7: 4 × 7 − 6 = 28 − 6 = 22. Not 41: that reads 4n as the number 47.

items.q: What is the value of 4 + 2n when n = 5?
items.e: Replace n with 5: 4 + 2 × 5 = 4 + 10 = 14. Not 30: that adds before multiplying (left to right).

items.q: Evaluate 7(n + 6) when n = 3.
items.e: Replace n with 3: 7 × (3 + 6) = 7 × 9 = 63. Not 27: that multiplies only 3 by 7.

items.q: Find the value of n ÷ 2 + 6 when n = 16.
items.e: Replace n with 16: 16 ÷ 2 + 6 = 8 + 6 = 14. Not 2: that adds before dividing.

items.q: What is the value of (n + 4) ÷ 2 when n = 28?
items.e: Replace n with 28: (28 + 4) ÷ 2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16. Not 30: that skips the parentheses.

items.q: Evaluate n2 + 6 when n = 7.
items.e: Replace n with 7: 72 + 6 = 49 + 6 = 55. Not 20: that reads 72 as 2 × 7.

items.q: Find the value of 2n2 when n = 3.
items.e: Replace n with 3: 2 × 32 = 2 × 9 = 18. Not 36: that squares 2 too, but only 3 is squared.

items.q: What is the value of n3 when n = 5?
items.e: Replace n with 5: 53 = 125. Not 15: that reads 53 as 3 × 5.

items.q: Evaluate 43 − 2n when n = 7.
items.e: Replace n with 7: 43 − 2 × 7 = 43 − 14 = 29. Not 287: that subtracts before multiplying.

items.q: Find the value of n(n + 2) when n = 5.
items.e: Replace n with 5: 5 × (5 + 2) = 5 × 7 = 35. Not 27: that skips the parentheses.

items.q: What is the value of 42 ÷ n + 8 when n = 6?
items.e: Replace n with 6: 42 ÷ 6 + 8 = 7 + 8 = 15. Not 3: that adds before dividing.

items.q: Evaluate 3x + 6y when x = 9 and y = 7.
items.e: Replace x with 9 and y with 7: 3 × 9 + 6 × 7 = 27 + 6 × 7 = 27 + 42 = 69. Not 75: that switches the values of x and y.

items.q: Find the value of xy − 5 when x = 9 and y = 8.
items.e: Replace x with 9 and y with 8: 9 × 8 − 5 = 72 − 5 = 67. Not 12: that adds x and y instead of multiplying.

items.q: What is the value of 6(x − y) when x = 15 and y = 2?
items.e: Replace x with 15 and y with 2: 6 × (15 − 2) = 6 × 13 = 78. Not 88: that multiplies only 15 by 6.

items.q: Evaluate x2 + y2 when x = 4 and y = 3.
items.e: Replace x with 4 and y with 3: 42 + 32 = 16 + 32 = 16 + 9 = 25. Not 49: that adds before squaring.

items.q: Find the value of 6x + y ÷ 2 when x = 4 and y = 14.
items.e: Replace x with 4 and y with 14: 6 × 4 + 14 ÷ 2 = 24 + 14 ÷ 2 = 24 + 7 = 31. Not 19: that adds before dividing.

items.q: Luis says 3n + 4 = 39 when n = 5. What mistake did he make?
items.e: 3n means 3 × n, not the digits 3 and 5 side by side: 3 × 5 + 4 = 15 + 4 = 19. Luis used 35 + 4 = 39.

items.q: Ava says 2n2 = 36 when n = 3. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The exponent goes with n only. Square first, then multiply: 2 × 32 = 2 × 9 = 18. Ava found (2 × 3)2 = 62 = 36.

items.q: Movie tickets cost $12 each. There is a $5 online fee for the whole order. Which expression shows the cost of t tickets?
items.e: Each ticket is $12, so t tickets cost 12t. The $5 fee is paid once: 12t + 5. 12(t + 5) would charge the fee for every ticket.

items.q: Sofia reads p pages each day for 6 days. Then she reads 20 more pages. Which expression shows how many pages she reads in all?
items.e: 6 days of p pages is 6p. Then add the 20 pages once: 6p + 20.

items.q: 4 friends share the cost of a pizza equally. The pizza costs c dollars. Which expression shows how much each friend pays?
items.e: Sharing equally means dividing the cost by 4: c ÷ 4. 4 ÷ c divides 4 by the cost, which is backward.

items.q: Harper is 3 years older than her brother. Her brother is b years old. Which expression shows Harper’s age?
items.e: Older means more years, so add 3 to the brother’s age: b + 3. 3b would mean 3 times as old.

items.q: Aaliyah has c trading cards. Ava has 5 fewer than twice as many cards as Aaliyah. Which expression shows how many cards Ava has?
items.e: Twice as many as Aaliyah is 2c. 5 fewer than that is 2c − 5. 5 − 2c has the order backward.

items.q: At noon it is 68°F. The temperature drops 2°F each hour. Which expression shows the temperature h hours after noon?
items.e: In h hours it drops 2h degrees. Take that away from 68: 68 − 2h. 68 + 2h would make it warmer.

items.q: A square garden has sides that are s feet long. Which expression shows the length of fence needed to go around it?
items.e: Going around means the perimeter. A square has 4 equal sides: 4s. s2 is the area, not the perimeter.

items.q: A phone plan costs $25 a month plus $3 for each gigabyte (GB) of data used. Which expression shows the cost for a month with g GB?
items.e: $3 for each of g GB is 3g. Add the $25 once: 25 + 3g. 25g + 3 puts the numbers on the wrong parts.

items.q: 4 friends order a pizza that costs p dollars and pay a $6 delivery fee. They split the total equally. Which expression shows what each friend pays?
items.e: The total is p + 6, and the whole total is split, so it goes in parentheses: (p + 6) ÷ 4. p + 6 ÷ 4 would split only the fee.

items.q: Liam read n pages on Monday and twice as many pages on Tuesday. Which expression shows how many pages he read on both days?
items.e: Monday is n pages and Tuesday is 2n pages. Add them: n + 2n, which is 3n. 2n counts only Tuesday.

items.q: Movie tickets cost $12 each, plus a $5 fee for the whole order. Use 12t + 5 to find the cost of 4 tickets.
items.e: Expression: 12t + 5. Replace t with 4: 12 × 4 + 5 = 48 + 5 = 53. Not $108: the fee is paid once, not for every ticket.

items.q: A taxi ride costs $3 plus $2.50 for each mile. Write an expression for m miles and find the cost of an 8-mile ride.
items.e: Expression: 3 + 2.5m. Replace m with 8: 3 + 2.5 × 8 = 3 + 20 = 23. Not $44.00: that adds 3 + 2.50 before multiplying.

items.q: Zoe has $40 and saves $8 each week. Write an expression for w weeks and find how much she has after 6 weeks.
items.e: Expression: 40 + 8w. Replace w with 6: 40 + 8 × 6 = 40 + 48 = 88. Not $288: that adds 40 + 8 before multiplying.

items.q: At a bake sale, cookies cost $0.75 each. Write an expression for c cookies and find how much 24 cookies cost.
items.e: Expression: 0.75c. Replace c with 24: 0.75 × 24 = 18. Not $1,800.00: 0.75 is less than 1, so the cost must be less than 24 dollars.

items.q: A car travels at 60 miles per hour. Write an expression for h hours and find how far it goes in 3.5 hours.
items.e: Expression: 60h. Replace h with 3.5: 60 × 3.5 = 210. Not 180 miles: that leaves out the half hour.

items.q: 4 friends order a pizza for p dollars and pay a $6 delivery fee. They split the total equally. Use (p + 6) ÷ 4 to find what each pays when p = 22.
items.e: Expression: (p + 6) ÷ 4. Replace p with 22: (22 + 6) ÷ 4 = 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Not $23.50: that splits only the fee. Not $28.00: that is the total, not each share.

items.q: At noon it is 68°F. The temperature drops 2°F each hour. Use 68 − 2h to find the temperature 5 hours after noon.
items.e: Expression: 68 − 2h. Replace h with 5: 68 − 2 × 5 = 68 − 10 = 58. Not 78°F: the temperature drops, so subtract.

items.q: A gym charges a $15 sign-up fee and $20 each month. Write an expression for m months and find the cost for 9 months.
items.e: Expression: 15 + 20m. Replace m with 9: 15 + 20 × 9 = 15 + 180 = 195. Not $180: that forgets the sign-up fee.

items.q: Marcus reads p pages each weekday (5 days) and 40 pages on Saturday. Write an expression and find the pages he reads in the week when p = 25.
items.e: Expression: 5p + 40. Replace p with 25: 5 × 25 + 40 = 125 + 40 = 165. Not 125 pages: that forgets Saturday.

items.q: A field trip costs $150 for the bus plus $8 for each student. Write an expression for n students and find the cost for 32 students.
items.e: Expression: 150 + 8n. Replace n with 32: 150 + 8 × 32 = 150 + 256 = 406. Not $5,056: that adds 150 + 8 before multiplying.
